A1.justification: Both PDFs are readable 24-page versions of the same LDHD generalization work. Their main text, equations, Figures 1–8 and Appendices A–E support a complete comparison.

before.justification: v2 reports original GPT-2 experiments on copying, arithmetic and ParityCoT, including RPE-Square and RPE-Absolute evaluations in Figure 2 and Appendix E.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and their length-generalization accuracy results in Figure 2 and Appendix E, Figures 3–8.

M1.justification: RFMP, PLAA and its APE/GRPE variants, RPE-Square in Section 5.2, and RPE-Absolute in Appendix E.2 retain the same definitions, components and procedures.

E1.justification: Both evaluate unaligned Copy, URF Addition, ParityCoT, Multiplication (1 * N), Division (N/1), and AdditionMod10. The task coverage and input formats are unchanged.

E2.justification: Figure 2 retains RPE versus RPE-Square. Figures 3–7 retain RPE, RoPE, NoPE, ALiBi and Abacus as RPE-Square comparators, while Figure 8 retains RPE versus RPE-Absolute.

E3.justification: Figures 2–8 and Appendices D.2–E retain the same sampling, training/test scales, accuracy metrics and model settings, including the 1,000-step copy and 20,000/200,000-step addition experiments.

E4.justification: The digitwise addition analysis in Figure 2(d) and the length-dependent evaluation curves are unchanged. No ablation, sensitivity analysis, robustness test or case study is added, removed or revised.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty bands. Statistical reporting practices are unchanged.

E6.justification: All experimental curves in Figures 2–8 match, including digitwise addition accuracy and the appendix comparisons. No numerical result, result entry, ranking or qualitative finding changes.

T1.justification: Definitions 1–7, Theorems 1–4, Corollaries 1–2, and the background, derivations and proofs in Appendices A–C are unchanged. Cross-reference and typesetting edits do not alter mathematical content.

C1.justification: The abstract, Section 1.1 and conclusion retain the same LDHD framework, inductive-bias results, CoT interpretation and positional-embedding contributions, without changing their scope or strength.

C2.justification: Both retain the explanations of unaligned-format failures, CoT's latent-space effect and the inductive-bias/expressiveness tradeoff. Section 6 retains the limitation that the theory concerns simplified models.

D1.justification: Appendices D.2–E retain identical data-generation instructions, tokenization details, GPT-2 implementation information, optimizer settings and hardware disclosure, including two RTX 3090 GPUs. No code or data access information changes.

R1.justification: Section 2 and the reference list retain the same cited works and positioning relative to prior length-generalization and inductive-bias research.

P1.justification: Four internal references change 'Appendix' to 'Section': B, B.1, D.1 and D.2. The arXiv version/date stamp is updated; the narrative and section order remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Minor local mathematical typesetting and spacing changes are visible, particularly on page 12. Figures 1–8 retain the same graphics, axes, legends, captions and placement.

improvement.justification: v3 preserves v2's scientific content, proofs, experimental evidence, reproducibility details and limitations. The four cross-reference wording changes, updated arXiv stamp and minor typesetting adjustments produce no meaningful net difference in clarity or scientific quality.
